en.name: Canola oil
en.summary: Canola oil keeps 1 year from purchase in a cool dark cupboard with the cap tight. It fails by going rancid rather than by growing anything, and light, heat, air and time are the four things that decide how fast.
en.pantry: 1 year from purchase, cool, dark and capped. Canola is a refined oil, which means the free fatty acids and most of the minor compounds have been stripped out, and that is why it keeps better than an unrefined nut or seed oil and stands up to frying. It is still an oil, though: it oxidises on contact with oxygen, faster in the light and faster when warm, and the headspace in a half-empty bottle is a supply of oxygen that grows every time you pour. The cupboard directly above the hob is the worst storage spot in the kitchen — the one that is warm all day, every day.
en.fridge: No refrigerated timeline is published for canola oil, and for a bottle in weekly use the fridge is unnecessary. It does slow oxidation, so it is a reasonable place for a very large bottle you are working through slowly, but the oil will cloud and thicken in the cold — harmless, and it clears again at room temperature. A cool cupboard away from the stove gets you most of the same benefit without the inconvenience.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published for canola oil and freezing is pointless. Oil does not set solid the way water does, so nothing is gained, and a bottle taken in and out of a cold place collects condensation. Water in an oil bottle is a real problem, because it gives spoilage organisms a foothold in a food that otherwise offers them nothing.
en.thawing: Let a chilled bottle stand at room temperature until it is clear and pours freely. Do not warm oil on the hob or in hot water — heat is one of the things that ages it.
spoilage: A sharp, crayon or paint-like smell — rancid oil, and decisive.
A bitter, scratchy finish at the back of the throat.
A thick, sticky film on the outside of the bottle or around the cap, which is oxidised oil polymerising.
Colour noticeably darker than when the bottle was opened.
tips: Buy a bottle you will finish within a few months, not the biggest one on the shelf.
Never store oil in the cupboard above the hob.
Wipe the neck and cap so a sticky ring does not build up.
Do not pour used frying oil back into the fresh bottle; keep it separately.

faq.q: How long does canola oil last?
faq.a: 1 year from purchase in a cool dark cupboard with the cap tight.

faq.q: Does canola oil need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: No. Refrigeration slows oxidation and suits a very large bottle used slowly, but the oil clouds and thickens in the cold. A cool cupboard away from the stove is enough.

faq.q: How can you tell if canola oil has gone off?
faq.a: Smell it. A sharp, crayon or paint-like note means it is rancid, and it will taste bitter and scratchy. That is a quality failure rather than a pathogen risk.

zh.name: 芥花油
zh.summary: 芥花油自購買日起，放陰涼避光的櫃子、瓶蓋鎖緊，可放 1 年。它的失敗方式是油耗而不是長東西，而決定速度快慢的是光、熱、空氣和時間這四件事。
zh.pantry: 自購買日起 1 年，陰涼、避光、鎖緊瓶蓋。芥花油是精煉油，也就是游離脂肪酸和大部分微量成分都已經被去掉，這正是它比未精煉的堅果油或種子油耐放、也更耐油炸的原因。但它終究是油：碰到氧氣就會氧化，光線下更快、溫度高更快；而半空瓶子裡的那段頂空，就是一個每倒一次就變大的氧氣供應。爐台正上方那個櫃子是全廚房最糟的存放位置——因為那裡每天整天都是熱的。
zh.fridge: 芥花油沒有公布的冷藏期限；而對一瓶每週都在用的油來說，冷藏也沒有必要。冷藏確實能拖慢氧化，所以一瓶很大、用得很慢的油放冷藏是合理的；但低溫下油會變濁、變稠——無害，回到室溫就清了。遠離爐火的陰涼櫃子，大部分好處都拿得到，又不會那麼麻煩。
zh.freezer: 芥花油沒有公布的冷凍期限，冷凍也沒有意義。油不像水那樣會凍成硬塊，所以什麼也沒得到；而一瓶在低溫處進進出出的油只會一直結露。油瓶裡有水是真正的問題，因為它在一個本來什麼都不提供的食物裡，給了腐敗菌一個立足點。
zh.thawing: 把冰過的瓶子放室溫，等它恢復清澈、倒得順即可。不要拿去爐火上或泡熱水加溫——熱正是讓它老化的原因之一。
spoilage: 聞起來刺鼻、像蠟筆或油漆味——油耗了，而且是決定性的。
入口後喉頭有苦味和刮喉感。
瓶身外側或瓶蓋周圍有一層黏稠的膜，那是氧化的油在聚合。
顏色比剛開瓶時明顯變深。
tips: 買幾個月內用得完的容量，不要挑架上最大瓶的。
絕對不要把油放在爐台上方的櫃子。
每次倒完擦一下瓶口和瓶蓋，才不會積出一圈黏膜。
用過的炸油不要倒回新油瓶，要另外裝。

faq.a: 自購買日起，陰涼避光、瓶蓋鎖緊，1 年。
不用。冷藏能拖慢氧化，適合用得很慢的大瓶裝，但低溫下會變濁變稠。放遠離爐火的陰涼櫃子就夠了。
聞一下。刺鼻、像蠟筆或油漆的味道就是油耗，吃起來會苦、會刮喉嚨。那是品質問題，不是病原菌風險。
